parsed.summary: The file asserts three results. First, the corrected Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture is false (`not_erdos_180`). Second, there is a finite nonempty family F of connected, bipartite, non-acyclic graphs with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3-1/48}), ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3} eventually for every F ∈ F, and F not compact (`compactnessCounterexample_bigO`). Third, a quantitative version with an explicit bound e(G)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for every F-free host G, for all n. The most important caveat: `quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample` contains the conjunct `(0 : ℤ) < 1 / 48`. In ℤ, 1/48 truncates to 0, so this conjunct reads 0 < 0, which is false. That theorem is therefore false as written and cannot be correctly proved, so either the statement is broken or the claimed proof needs scrutiny. The other two targets look faithful.

glossary.plain: A finite simple graph given as a vertex count plus a SimpleGraph on Fin order.
The host G contains no member of the family as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph.
glossary.note: Mathlib `Free A B` = ¬ A.IsContained B, i.e. no injective copy, matching subgraph containment.

glossary.plain: ex(n,F): the maximum number of edges over F-free graphs on Fin n; equals 0 if no host is F-free.
glossary.note: The empty sup (= 0) would arise only if F contains the 0-vertex graph, which is acyclic and hence excluded for cyclic families. The empty graph on Fin n is always free otherwise.

glossary.standard_concept: family of graphs each containing a cycle

glossary.plain: ∃ F ∈ F, ∃ C > 0, for all sufficiently large n, ex(n,F) ≤ C·ex(n,F).
Every finite nonempty family all of whose members contain cycles is compact.
For each F ∈ F, eventually c·n^{4/3} ≤ ex(n,F), with one common c.
glossary.note: A uniform c is equivalent to per-member constants because the family is finite.

lean_claims.plain: The corrected compactness conjecture is false.

There exist a family F and c, C > 0 such that: F is nonempty; every member is connected, bipartite and contains a cycle; eventually ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3} for all F ∈ F; for all n and every F-free G on n vertices, e(G)^16 ≤ C·n^21; ex(n,F)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n; (0:ℤ) < 1/48 (false in ℤ); 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48 in ℝ; F is not compact; and the conjecture fails.

There exist a nonempty family F of connected, bipartite, cyclic graphs and c > 0 such that each member eventually has ex(n,F) ≥ c·n^{4/3`, ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) as n → ∞, F is not compact, and the conjecture fails.

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) and ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F; in particular no member satisfies (1), disproving compactness.
There is a connected bipartite 2-degenerate H with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} eventually.

coverage.why: All components of (2) and the failure of (1) are stated.
Otherwise stronger than the paper (explicit bound for all n), but it contains the false conjunct (0:ℤ) < 1/48.

flags.explanation: `(0 : ℤ) < 1 / 48` uses integer division, so 1/48 = 0 and the conjunct is 0 < 0, which is false. The whole existential is therefore false and should be unprovable. If a proof was accepted, investigate it. The intended claim ε = 1/48 > 0 would need ℚ or ℝ.
The bound e(G)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n (not just large n) is stronger than the paper's O-bound. This is fine, apart from F1.

lint_verdicts.why: edgeFinset of a graph on Fin n is finite, so the card is the true edge count.
Integer division makes 1/48 = 0, so the conjunct is false.
This is the finite edge count of the host graph.
The exponent is computed by exact real division.
